chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and said, 'O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' So, among what he advised him was that he said: 'Meet your brother with a cheerful face.'
ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet's advice on how to greet one's brother?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on goodly cheerfulness, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) emphasizes that a radiant countenance is a fundamental aspect of Islamic etiquette and spiritual warmth. It reflects the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) as an extension of faith, where inner sincerity manifests in outward pleasantness, fostering brotherhood and social harmony within the community.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboubn, from Hisham Bin Salim, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup style="font-weight: normal">asws</sup> having said:

‘A man came over to Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>, so he said, ‘O Rasool-Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup>! Advise me’. So, among what he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> advised him was that he<sup style="font-weight: normal">saww</sup> said: ‘Meet your brother with a cheerful face’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub from Hisham ibn Salim from abu Basir from abu Ja’far (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Once a man came to the Messenger of Allah, saying, ‘O Messenger of Allah, confer upon me good advice.’ Of the advice given to him was this: ‘Meet your brethren (fellow human beings) with open and delightful face.’”
